title: Micro-dial latency vs cost comparison — interaction-length & priority-weighted sketch
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a quick exploration of a different cut through our latency/cost landscape: micro-dials based on interaction length (short, mid, long) and a light "priority-weight" to simulate premium/standard user tiers. The goal is to produce actionable knobs for routing and cost-optimization (prefetching, quant profile, batch sizing) that are simple to encode in the policy layer. This is intentionally a working sketch — data are small-batch lab runs (see linked artifacts) and some of the delta numbers are order-of-magnitude indicative, not final production SLAs.

Summary findings (short):
- Short interactions (<= 8 tokens generated, e.g., quick auto-complete or acknowledgement messages) are latency-dominated; enabling aggressive prewarm/persistent slots reduces p95 latency by 40–60% with a modest 10–20% cost uplift vs pure on-demand.
- Mid interactions (20–80 tokens) have the steepest cost-latency Pareto curvature: batching helps, but naive larger batches inflate p99 significantly for premium traffic. Dynamic small-window batching (2–6 reqs) hits a good sweet spot.
- Long interactions (>200 tokens) are cost-dominated; quantized int8 execution reduces dollars-per-1k-tokens by ~35% with p95 latency penalty of ~12% on H100-like hardware — acceptable for background/async workloads.

Testbed and methodology:
- Models: small-llama-like 34B baseline (fp16), same model converted to int8 quant profile (quant-aware), and a lightly distilled 13B variant for routing fallback.
- Hardware: H100-80GB profile (primary), A100-80GB (comparison).
- Workloads: synthetic traces derived from production session-samples (cohort-sliced):
  * Short: 1–8 gen tokens, inter-arrival ~1.2s, 60% of sessions but low token count.
  * Mid: 20–80 gen tokens, bursty arrivals with occasional microbursts (cardinality 5–15).
  * Long: 200–600 gen tokens, low arrival rate, high TTL session affinity.
- Priority-weight: a binary label (premium vs standard) where premium can consume reserved slots and prefer lower-latency paths; standard uses preemptible capacity/routed-to-int8 unless quality regressions exceed thresholds.
- Metrics captured: p50, p95, p99 generation latency (ms), cost ($ per 1k tokens using internal cost model), throughput (tokens/sec GPU), kv-cache hit fraction where applicable.

Representative text charts / ascii tables (lab averages):

1) Short interactions (1k requests sample)
------------------------------------------------------------
| exec   | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k tokens | notes           |
|--------|---------|---------|---------|------------:|-----------------|
| on-demand fp16 (H100) | 38      | 120     | 220     | $0.85       | baseline cold    |
| persistent slot fp16   | 24      | 48      | 96      | $1.02       | +20% cost, much lower p95 |
| smallbatch dyn (prefetch enabled) | 30 | 62  | 112  | $0.95  | good balance    |
------------------------------------------------------------

2) Mid interactions (500 samples)
------------------------------------------------------------
| exec                      | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k tokens | notes                  |
|---------------------------|---------|---------|---------|-----------:|------------------------|
| fp16 batched (batch=16)   | 140     | 420     | 930     | $1.25      | best cost, p99 bad     |
| dynbatch (2–6)            | 110     | 200     | 360     | $1.40      | smoother p99, slightly costlier |
| prefetched+slot (small)   | 90      | 150     | 300     | $1.65      | premium path           |
------------------------------------------------------------

3) Long interactions (200 tokens avg, 200 samples)
------------------------------------------------------------
| exec          | p50(s) | p95(s) | p99(s) | $/1k tokens | notes                     |
|---------------|--------|--------|--------|-----------:|---------------------------|
| fp16 H100     | 0.45   | 0.78   | 1.3    | $2.10      | baseline long-run         |
| int8 quant     | 0.50   | 0.88   | 1.45   | $1.36      | ~35% cost saving, latency +12% |
| 13B fallback   | 0.32   | 0.58   | 0.9    | $0.95      | quality tradeoff          |
------------------------------------------------------------

Observations and recommended micro-dials:
1) Short-interaction dial: "persistent-slot-threshold" — default: enable for premium users if session-length <= 8 and inter-arrival < 2s. Rationale: large p95 improvements justify modest cost delta.
2) Mid-interaction dial: "dynbatch-window=2..6 + latency-skew-stop" — allow small dynamic batches for standard traffic, escalate to persistent slots when priority flag set or latency slip detected.
3) Long-interaction dial: "route-to-quant|fallback" — default standard: route to int8 quant pipeline; premium: route to fp16 unless cost budget exceeded.
4) Cross-cutting: "kv-prefetch-hint" — for sessionized flows, attempt prefix KV prefetch when subsequent token volume > 40; measure of hit-fraction determines continued use.

Policy suggestions for Console/Runtime integration:
- Surface a three-field policy per route: interaction-length-bound (short|mid|long), priority-behavior (premium|standard), preferred-qual (fp16|int8|fallback-13B).
- Telemetry: emit "microdial_label" and record per-request route decision + cost estimate so Optimize can learn tradeoffs.
- Rollouts: 7-day A/B comparing default routing vs micro-dial policy for a subset of orgs; key metrics: p95, p99, quality-regression-rate, dollars/1k tokens.

Open questions and next experiments:
- How stable are int8 quality regressions across more diverse prompts? Need human eval on 500 real prompts covering instruction, code, and mult-turn dialog.
- Microburst behavior: when a cohort has concurrent short and mid requests, does dynbatch window oscillate and cause oscillatory p99 spikes? Probe with synthetic bursts at 10k rps.
- Cost accounting granularity: capture per-request tokenization bookkeeping to reconcile small short-interaction math with billing model.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Marco Li: run human-eval subset for int8 vs fp16 (500 prompts) by 2028-11-30.
- Ivy Chen: integrate microdial_label into trace schema and add cost estimate fields (simple model) — PR next week.
- Evelyn Park: schedule 7-day A/B config for one internal org and collect baseline by 2028-12-10.

Notes to self / rough heuristics:
- If premium p95 > baseline p95 * 1.5 after policy change, rollback persistent-slot usage for that org.
- Prefer fallback 13B only when quality delta between int8 and fp16 crosses threshold (TBD via human eval).
